newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares spike up to record high close.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares spike up to record high close.

text.p: Dutch blue chips nudged up to a new all-time closing high on Tuesday, buoyed by favourable U.S.
December consumer prices, a robust dollar and a firmer Wall Street opening.

The AEX index of leading Dutch shares battered through key resistance at 655 to close the session up 5.07 points (+0.78 pct) at 657.83. The previous record close of January 6 was 652.84. Earlier it touched a record intraday high of 657.98.
Dealers said that having breached resistance, the index was in uncharted territory. "We can't predict where it will end," one said.
"After 655 -- which we thought was major resistance -- we don't have any reference," said another.

Double-digit preliminary profit growth figures from Dutch companies such as copier maker Oce van der Grinten -- due to replace foods group CSM in the AEX index from February 24 -- had also persuaded investors the only way was up, dealers said.
"Private investors are certainly quite willing to take exposure in the market," one said. "There is scope for a further rally, with high-techs seeming to capture the imagination."
Semiconductors equipment maker ASM and chip tester Rood Testhouse both built on Monday's gains.
Dealers said the AEX surge, led by a rise in dollar-sensitive stocks which are heavily weighted on the index, had caught the options market on the hop.
"There is massive open interest in calls at the 650 level ahead of Friday's options expiry," a dealer noted.
He said naked call writers scrabbling to cover themselves would lead to basket buying on the cash market, thereby further fuelling the index rise.
Another dealer predicted the index could push another 20 points higher next week. "We saw a similar pattern at the December expiry, when options players were thrown by Greenspan."
Remarks then by chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan that markets were coasting at irrationally high levels sparked a brief dip and subsequent bull reaction, he said.
Dealers said Tuesday's overall volumes had however remained relatively low, except in Royal Dutch, Unilever and the banks, where trade had been brisk.
Royal Dutch ended up 0.80 at 310.50 after spending the early part of the session in negative territory on news of lower overnight oil prices.
Unilever jumped 6.30 guilders to 308.80, fuelled by demand from a big foreign buyer, dealers said.
Financial services group ING added 0.90 guilders to 65.30, while ABN Amro surged 3.40 guilders to 116.00.
